messages.subject: scatterplots and subsets
parts:
Hi, I'm trying to do a scatterplot with both a trendline and labeled
datapoints. Unfortunately, while I can get a trendline or labels
trying to combine both usually results in a crash or some message that
says 'NaN'

mylist <- read.csv(file.choose())
library(ggplot2)
df2 = data.frame(control =mylist$controlvalue, experiment=mylist
$expvalue, labcolumn=mylist$labelcolumn)
basicplot<-ggplot(data=df2, aes(x=control, y=experiment,
label=labcolumn))+geom_point()+geom_text()
basicplot<-basicplot+stat_smooth(method="lm")
basicplot

ps
Once I get this to work I need to do some subset work
How could I color the points by different subsets (ie 1-10 green 11-20
blue etc) and have these groups listed on the legend. And have two
graphs top and bottom?

Thanks

parts:
On 2012-Mar-15, at 02:39 , Ace wrote:
>
> Hi, I'm trying to do a scatterplot with both a trendline and labeled
> datapoints. Unfortunately, while I can get a trendline or labels
> trying to combine both usually results in a crash or some message that
> says 'NaN'
>
> mylist <- read.csv(file.choose())
> library(ggplot2)
> df2 = data.frame(control =mylist$controlvalue, experiment=mylist
> $expvalue, labcolumn=mylist$labelcolumn)
> basicplot<-ggplot(data=df2, aes(x=control, y=experiment,
> label=labcolumn))+geom_point()+geom_text()
> basicplot<-basicplot+stat_smooth(method="lm")
> basicplot

It's difficult without actual data to work with. Please provide a dummy, example dataset.

I would guess that this:

ggplot(data=df2, aes(x=control, y=experiment)) + geom_point() + geom_text(aes(label=labcolumn)) + geom_smooth(method="lm")

should be working.

> ps
> Once I get this to work I need to do some subset work
> How could I color the points by different subsets (ie 1-10 green 11-20
> blue etc) and have these groups listed on the legend.

You need to have a column which defines the subset number such as

subsetNb control experiment label
1 2.3 2.5 foo
1 2.4 2.3 bar
1 2.7 2.7 bar
2 2.2 1.7 foo
2 1.9 2.4 bar
…

and then map it to colour

ggplot(data=df2, aes(x=control, y=experiment, colour=subsetNb)) + geom_point() + geom_text(aes(label=labcolumn)) + geom_smooth(method="lm")

> And have two
> graphs top and bottom?

What would be the top and bottom graphs?
